title: Beavers: Nature’s River Engineers
hook: Beavers, the world’s largest rodents, reshape rivers with astonishing engineering skill, creating

scenes.narration: Beavers, the world’s largest rodents, reshape rivers with astonishing engineering skill, creating thriving wetlands that support countless hidden species.
Both the Eurasian beaver (Castor fiber) and the North American beaver (Castor canadensis) belong to the genus Castor, family Castoridae.
Modern beavers are prolific ecosystem engineers, dramatically altering landscapes through tree harvesting and dam construction that reshape water flow worldwide.
Beavers’ renowned woodcutting behavior supplies the material for their dams and lodges, showcasing remarkable engineering instincts that benefit river ecosystems.
These rodents have colonized every continent except Antarctica, thriving in deserts, tundra, forests, and wetlands alike, demonstrating extraordinary adaptability today.
Their global distribution reflects a slow molecular evolution, as mitochondrial genomes reveal timing of beaver speciation across millions of years.
Genetic studies place beavers within a mouse‑related clade, closely linked to kangaroo‑rat families in the Castorimorpha group, supporting evolutionary connections.
Thus, beavers act as natural architects, their engineering reshaping rivers and fostering dynamic ecosystems across the planet for future generations.
